title: Ink Storm
tagline: A living ink painting. Stir it forever and the detail never smears.

paper.title: A neural characteristic mapping method: Lagrangian PINNs based on flow maps for transport-dominated problems

novelty: No known implementation (not verified): a full-screen pressure-projected fluid toy whose marbled artwork is pulled back through a GPU-advected flow map, so filaments stay sharp indefinitely.
description: A full-screen GPU fluid painting: drag to stir procedural marbled art, pour glowing ink, switch palettes and patterns, and save your swirl. The artwork is evaluated through a backward flow map, so fine filaments survive stirring that would blur an ordinary dye field.
howItWorks: A WebGL2 stable-fluids solver (advection, vorticity confinement, pressure projection) runs at about 200 cells high. A 32-bit backward flow map at up to 1100 pixels high is advected through the same velocity field, and every pixel looks up the procedural marble pattern at its pulled-back position, so detail is never resampled away. Poured ink is a separate classically advected layer. The paper learns flow maps with Lagrangian PINNs; this demo uses the classical characteristic-map idea only and runs no neural network.
controls: Drag to stir. Double-tap or double-click for a vortex burst. Pour toggles glowing ink under your finger. Pick a palette, cycle Pattern, Reset, or Save a PNG. Leave it alone and it stirs itself.
